objective: Investigate newly available laboratory result LAB-0225; assess scope, plausible explanations and human-reviewed next steps.

report.assessment: LAB-0225 is a newly available (2024-12-01T12:00:00Z) relative_bioburden_signal result on an upstream process sample of BATCH-075 (Famotidine Injection, USP; sterile solution for injection; LINE-A): 1.23 action-limit ratio, i.e., 23% above the 1.0 action limit and above the 0.7 alert limit, with status 'action' - the highest lab result in the scoped package. Two further same-morning BATCH-075 signals were at alert level (PRE-LAB-001 0.79, collected 10:45Z; EM-0075 0.71 in the process support area, 10:50Z), so three contemporaneous streams (collected within 10 minutes) show elevated microbial signal; no temporal trend is supported because collection order runs 1.23 -> 0.79 -> 0.71. All four BATCH-075 historian parameters on the incident date are within expected ranges with normal severity, the only operator event is a routine check, and no deviation or hold record exists for BATCH-075. Scope: the signal is isolated to BATCH-075 on the current date; the same limit was exceeded historically by SYN-0004 (1.08, Feb) and SYN-0014 (1.06, Apr). Plausible explanations remain open: true process bioburden (supported by multi-stream elevation), laboratory/testing artifact (unconfirmed single result, no replicate/method records), environmental contribution (EM alert; historical lab+EM co-elevation pattern), or equipment condition (PUMP-02 historical excursion; no current excursion). Maintenance/work-order content, operator events beyond OP-0075, and source_review.pdf were NOT searched before retrieval budget exhaustion and remain explicit gaps. Proposed next steps are human-reviewed: QA review and investigation decision, batch hold verification, confirmatory retest with method review, and EM/maintenance follow-up. No disposition, release or CAPA is made or implied here; final severity is policy-derived. Advisory severity proposal: MEDIUM.

report.cross_scope_synthesis: Shared patterns: (1) All 1049 deterministic screening flags are identical 'missing_source_time' clock-quality flags on lab result/limit rows across microbiology, LIMS export, EM and historian sources - an acquisition artifact of rows lacking a source clock cell, not a process fault; ordering must use explicit calendar cells. (2) Lab values are duplicated across microbiology_results.xlsx and lims_export.csv and echoed in lims_review_local.csv and the scanned PDF, indicating one propagated result entry rather than independent confirmations. (3) Historically, the three batches with the highest micro results (SYN-0029, SYN-0032, SYN-0018) each also show an above-alert EM value, and BATCH-075 reproduces this lab+EM co-elevated pattern on 2024-12-01 (micro 1.23 action; EM 0.71 alert; PRE-LAB 0.79 alert). Exceptions: SYN-0004 and SYN-0014 exceeded the same action limit in Feb/Apr 2024 without any above-alert EM value, and PUMP-02's single high-severity excursion (PROC-0058, SYN-0015, 2024-04-05) did not coincide with an above-alert lab result for that batch. Equipment parameters for BATCH-075 on the incident date are all in range with normal severity, so no concurrent process-parameter excursion is documented. Limits of the synthesis: all results are single reported values without raw replicates (SEM columns are source summaries); no assay-method, recipe, controller or cleaning records were retrievable; maintenance/work-order content, operator events beyond OP-0075, and source_review.pdf were not searched before retrieval budget exhaustion (not_searched, not none_found); OCR lines are unverified; and the package manifest declares all records to be reconstructed synthetic data. The evidence supports contemporaneous multi-stream elevation around BATCH-075 sampling with an unconfirmed single action-level result; it does not establish cause, and the log end at the cutoff does not prove absence of later results.
